🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO IS AMONG THE 5 MOST-TRUSTED GOVERNMENTS IN THE ENTIRE OECD

While the foreign press sells a country in chaos, the OECD just placed Mexico among its five nations where most people trust their national government: 53% — a full 13 points above the OECD average of 40%, behind only Switzerland, Iceland, Norway and Luxembourg. Trust runs highest among those who lived through the neoliberal years — 60% among people over 50. Satisfaction with public services climbed from 67% to 72% in two years.

🚨🇲🇽 WASHINGTON CALLS MEXICO THE FENTANYL THREAT — ITS OWN DEA LET HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF PILLS FLOOD NEW MEXICO

For years Washington branded Mexican cartels "foreign terrorists" and leaned on Mexico's sovereignty in the name of fentanyl. Now New Mexico's own governor, Michelle Lujan Grisham, is moving to sue the DEA after agents deliberately let hundreds of thousands of fentanyl pills reach the streets to "build bigger cases" — a tactic one DEA official, David Howell, warned back in 2023 had "poisoned our community." The poison was flowing from inside the house all along.

🇲🇽🏭 $82.5 BILLION HEADED FOR MEXICAN DATA CENTERS: THE AI BUILDOUT LANDS SOUTH OF THE BORDER

Mexico is on track to capture $82.5 billion in data-center investment between 2026 and 2031, according to the Mexican Data Centers Association (MexDC) — projected to create 98,366 jobs during construction and 35,430 permanent operating positions. Querétaro alone holds 72% of the projects. The global AI boom needs power, land, and proximity to the US market, and capital is betting Mexico delivers all three (El Economista).

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO OPENS A STERILE-FLY PLANT — AND DRAWS THE LINE ON WHO RUNS IT

Sheinbaum inaugurated a sterile screwworm-fly plant in Metapa, Chiapas — 100 million sterile insects a week to wipe out the livestock pest that shut the US cattle border. And she was explicit about sovereignty: the plant runs on Mexican personnel and is operated by Senasica, the national ag-safety agency, which hires the staff. "Cooperation between sovereign nations will always be more powerful than confrontation," she said.

🔥🇲🇽 THE PAN'S "111 IDEAS": SELL THE REFINERY, REVIVE SEGURO POPULAR, BUILD A MEGA-PRISON

The PAN rolled out 111 proposals, and Sheinbaum read them for exactly what they are: "The only thing they want is to return to the past of corruption and privileges." Among them — selling the Dos Bocas refinery, bringing back Seguro Popular, and building a mega-prison. On the health rollback she was blunt: "Do they want to return to a Seguro Popular that built 80 hospitals and left only empty shells?" Her verdict: "They aren't even innovative; their proposals are to return to the past."

🔥🇲🇽 THE NYT'S "MEXICAN GOVERNORS ARE US INFORMANTS" STORY — BUILT ON ANONYMOUS NOTHING

The New York Times claims at least a dozen Mexican governors and Morena legislators are secretly feeding intelligence to the US Justice Department. Sheinbaum's reply: "We don't know if it's true, because we have no information that anyone is cooperating with the US government to provide information." She noted the whole piece rests on "a source told me, who knows" sourcing — no names, no documents. Just a foreign paper floating the idea that Mexican officials answer to Washington.

🇲🇽🌎 84.5% OF MEXICO'S FARM EXPORTS DEPEND ON ONE BLOC — AND WASHINGTON KNOWS IT

First four months of 2026: Mexico exported $18.46 billion in agri-food products — and 84.5% of it ($15.6 billion) went to the US and Canada under the T-MEC, per the GCMA, leaving a $4.86 billion surplus with North America. Record numbers, yes. But also the structural risk Sheinbaum and AMLO have flagged for years: when one bloc absorbs the overwhelming majority of your food exports, that bloc holds the leverage — and Washington has shown it treats tariffs as a political weapon.

🔥🇲🇽 18 YEARS IN PRISON FOR A CRIME THAT NEVER HAPPENED: THE WALLACE CASE

Brenda Quevedo spent 18 years across four prisons — and still has no first-instance verdict — for the fabricated "Wallace" kidnapping, a case built on confessions extracted under torture. "They wanted me to sign a confession admitting to the murder; I didn't," she told La Jornada. Last year the Supreme Court annulled a co-accused's 43-year sentence after confirming it rested on testimony obtained through torture. A neoliberal-era media spectacle — a vanished "victim," and innocents tortured into signing.
